title: Polarization engineered all 2D Graphene/Ferroelectric hybrid for persistence-free photoresponse
authors: Navkiranjot Kaur Gill, Shaili Sett, Saloni Kakkar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Arindam Ghosh
abstract: Graphene-based van der Waals hybrid photodetectors typically work on trap-mediated photogating mechanism, exhibiting high sensitivity, but under-perform in the fast detection of repetitive optical signals. Designing photodetectors that are simultaneously fast and highly sensitive has therefore remained difficult. In this work, we realize both attributes by integrating atomically thin sliding ferroelectrics in the design architecture, thereby uniting semiconducting properties with intrinsic polarization fields capable of efficiently governing interfacial photocarrier dynamics. We report a bilayer graphene-bilayer MoS2 (with MoS2 in a rhombohedrally stacked (3R) configuration) van der Waals photodetector with edge-contacted dual-gated field-effect transistor architecture. The photo-induced modulation in spontaneous out-of-plane polarization of 3R-MoS2 and selective confinement of charge carriers in bilayer graphene under an out-of-plane displacement field results in a tunable persistence-free photoresponse. Here, the photoinduced polarization change in 3R-MoS2 produces an optically controlled gating effect that alters the electrostatic environment of bilayer graphene, resulting in a temperature-independent photoresponse with rapid response times of the order of 10's of milliseconds (limited by the measurement instrument). We demonstrate reproducible detection of optical signals and examine the photon-counting resolution of this structure in high-sensitivity regimes, where we determine its internal quantum efficiency to be 10 percent with minimum detectable photon number of 31 in single shot measurements. This work highlights the functionality of 3R-MoS2 in manipulating the interfacial charge dynamics and establishes the hybrid of graphene and ferroelectric 3R-MoS2 as a promising platform for ultra-sensitive optoelectronic devices.
summary: This work reports on a novel photodetector built from a Graphene/Ferroelectric (3R-MoS2) van der Waals hybrid. By exploiting the spontaneous polarization of the ferroelectric layer, the researchers achieved a tunable, persistence-free photoresponse in bilayer graphene. This breakthrough overcomes the trade-off between speed and sensitivity, establishing the platform for advanced optoelectronic devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is designing photodetectors that can achieve both high sensitivity and fast response times, overcoming limitations associated with trap-mediated photogating mechanisms.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a tunable, persistence-free photoresponse in a Graphene/Ferroelectric hybrid by utilizing the polarization field from 3R-MoS2 to optically gate bilayer graphene.
method: The study employed electrical and optoelectronic characterization techniques, including KPFM mapping, time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, and measuring transient photoresistance under varying illumination conditions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a van der Waals heterostructure comprising bilayer graphene (BLG) interfaced with a ferroelectric material, specifically bilayer MoS2 in the rhombohedrally stacked (3R) phase. This structure is configured as an edge-contacted dual-gated field-effect transistor.
key_observables: Photoresponse magnitude ($\Delta R$), relaxation timescales ($	au_A \approx 10$ ms), internal quantum efficiency ($\approx 10\%$), and the persistence of photo-induced changes under different doping regimes.
important_parameters: The response time is reported as being limited by the measurement instrument (tens of milliseconds); the mechanism relies on the intrinsic polarization field ($E_{i,P}$) from the ferroelectric layer.
main_assumptions: The rapid photoresponse in the hole-doped regime is attributed to a mechanism governed by polarization modulation rather than conventional trap-mediated charge trapping/detrapping processes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate KPFM potential mapping, PL spectra comparing 3R and 2H phases, time traces showing persistence-free response (especially in the hole-doped regime), and photon counting histograms confirming high sensitivity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the limitations of existing photodetectors; it then details the fabrication and characterization of the BLG/3R-MoS2 structure using multiple techniques (KPFM, PL); subsequently, it analyzes the photoresponse dynamics, highlighting the doping asymmetry that dictates whether the response is persistent or persistence-free.
why_interesting: While primarily an experimental condensed matter device physics paper, the control over interfacial charge dynamics via intrinsic polarization fields offers insights into engineered quantum interfaces relevant to open quantum systems and energy harvesting.
